{{Top|canon=Hilt-ring}}
[[File:LukeSkywalkerLightsaber-SWE.png|thumb|The hilt of Luke Skywalker's green lightsaber featured a belt ring attached to the pommel.]]
'''Belt rings''' were a [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] component that allowed the weapon to be attached to the wearer's [[Belt/Legends|belt]].<ref>''[[Star Wars: The Visual Dictionary]]'' {{C|Special Technology}}</ref> 

==History==
Belt-rings were commonly affixed at the base of the hilt, from which the lightsaber would hang with its [[blade emitter]] facing downward, such as [[Obi-Wan Kenobi's third lightsaber/Legends|those of Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and [[Anakin Skywalker's second lightsaber/Legends|Luke Skywalker]]. However, [[Darth Vader's lightsaber]] often had one positioned on its emitter shroud, and thus hanged facing upward.<ref name="A New Hope">{{Film|4}}</ref>
{{Stub}}

==Behind the scenes==
For the [[original trilogy]] of ''[[Star Wars]]'' films, a belt-hanger system was derived by mounting D-ring assemblies to the lightsaber props, often with rivets or screws.<ref name="WannaWanga">{{WebCite|url=https://wannawanga.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/03/SWLB_March_2020.pdf|text=The Complete Lightsaber Prop Guide (PDF)|archivedate=20250715003755}}</ref> In the [[prequel trilogy]], this system was dropped in favor of using Covertec wheels affixed to the hilts for belt attachment,<ref name="WannaWanga" /> although their in-universe role would be assigned to other functions, such as charging ports<ref>''[[Star Wars: Episode I: The Visual Dictionary]]'' {{C|Qui-Gon Jinn}} {{C|Obi-Wan Kenobi}}</ref> or power indicators.<ref>''[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith: The Visual Dictionary]]'' {{C|Darth Vader}}</ref>
